report.summary: Chunk 3 of 7: implements secret floor scan and envelope construction helpers for council bus.
risks: _scan_paths | low | Iterates over paths but uses secret_floor_rule(str(p), "") which passes empty text; if secret_floor_rule expects a file path, this may be incorrect. | Check secret_floor_rule signature in its definition.
_scan_turn | medium | Includes evidence paths again in texts after already scanned in _scan_paths; may cause duplicate scanning. | Confirm if duplicate scanning is intended or a bug.
_norm_evidence | medium | Assumes evidence dict must have exactly keys 'path' and 'sha256'; if future evidence items have extra keys, they are rejected. | Verify if this strictness is desired.
_norm_meta | low | Uses hardcoded default 'unknown' for cli_version, endpoint, transport; if these are never set, they become 'unknown'. | Check if 'unknown' is acceptable or should be None.
todos: Review _norm_evidence strictness for future evidence schema changes.

claims.text: PATH channel, one path at a time -- so a hit is attributable to one path and a diff that ADDS .env cannot hide inside a blob.
claims.why: The claim about diffs and .env hiding refers to behavior outside this chunk.

claims.text: CONTENT channel, one string at a time. path="" here is correct and is NOT the forbidden whole-prompt call: the path tier is run separately over every evidence path above, so it is never skipped.
claims.why: The claim about 'forbidden whole-prompt call' and 'path tier run separately' refers to code not in this chunk.

claims.text: Every free-text and every path channel of a turn. Returns the rule label that fired (a fixed string -- NEVER matched text), or None.
claims.why: The claim about rule label being a fixed string and not matched text refers to secret_floor_rule behavior not in this chunk.

claims.text: withheld: content channel ONLY (see the carve-out in the module docstring).
claims.why: The carve-out is in the module docstring, not in this chunk.

claims.text: sorted + deduped: a set of claims, not an ordered rendering (determinism).
claims.why: The code uses sorted({str(v) ...}) which sorts and deduplicates.

claims.text: evidence item {e!r} must be exactly {'path','sha256'} -- use evidence_ref(path, data)
claims.why: The code checks set(e) != {"path", "sha256"} and raises ValueError.

claims.text: evidence sha256 ... is not a 64-hex digest: an uncheckable citation is worse than none
claims.why: The code checks _SHA256_RE.match(sha) and raises ValueError.

observations.what: _scan_paths iterates over paths and calls secret_floor_rule with path and empty string.
_scan_turn includes evidence paths again in texts list after already scanning paths separately.
_norm_evidence enforces strict dict shape with exactly two keys.
_norm_meta uses hardcoded defaults for some fields.
_norm_class is partially defined; only signature visible.
